title: A Locker for the Mixtape
premise: Jonah Hartwell, a self-invisible coder at Northgate High, runs an anonymous gossip account that knows too much—until the school's legendary ghost begins leaving him handwritten notes in ink that shouldn't exist, each one naming secrets he never told anyone. Following the notes, he uncovers that the school board buried a scandal years ago: the death of a student, covered up to protect a beloved teacher and the board's own reputations, and the ghost is the student's sister testing whether Jonah will stay silent or speak. As the final audition for the school musical approaches—an audition the board will use to unveil a new arts wing built on the lie—Jonah must choose between the loyalty of the friends who shielded him and the truth that could free them all, ending with him broadcasting the buried records mid-audition and accepting the ghost's final note: his own name, written in ordinary ink, at last.
about_author: H. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former high school AV-club kid who spent more afternoons in detention than on stage. Hartwell writes stories about quiet kids who discover that silence is also a choice.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet Northgate High through the eyes of a boy who has engineered his own invisibility, posting school gossip as @hallwayghost while eating lunch in the AV closet. When his best friend Dev begs him to audition for the spring musical, Jonah deflects. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being nobody.

chapters.title: The Locker That Isn't Mine
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His jammed locker swings open to reveal an envelope addressed 'Jonah Hartwell' in shimmering violet ink that smears like wet paint but never dries. The note says: 'You know what happened to Marisol Vega. So do I.' He has never heard the name. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a flashback thread. He tests the ink—UV light, solvents, his own chemistry know-how—and it matches nothing. Researching Marisol Vega, he finds her name scrubbed from yearbooks and the school's digital archives with suspicious thoroughness. Emotional beat: obsession taking root.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Résumé
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, the musical's eager stage manager, narrates the legend of the Northgate Ghost, said to be a student who died in the old auditorium. Dev notices Jonah's distraction and worries he's relapsing into the anxiety spiral of freshman year. Emotional beat: friendship as quiet surveillance.

chapters.title: Second Note: The Board Photo
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A note in his gym locker shows a 2009 school board photo with one face inked out, captioned 'Ask why the arts wing is named for a man who never taught.' The board chair, Raymond Ostrander, is pushing the wing's dedication at the musical's final audition night. Emotional beat: the first map of the cover-up.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Things
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, editor of the school paper and the only student Ostrander fears, has her own file on the Vega case—her cousin was Marisol's best friend. She clocks Jonah's questions and offers an alliance; Jonah, terrified of exposure, lies to her. Emotional beat: the cost of distrust.

chapters.title: The Auditorium at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following a note's instructions, he breaks into the condemned old auditorium and finds Marisol's original drama trophy and a rehearsal tape. The ghost—or someone—watches him leave. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Static on the Tape
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Restoring the damaged tape, Jonah hears a young Marisol rehearsing a monologue, then a heated argument with a teacher—Mr. Aldous, now vice principal—about 'what happened at the lake house.' The tape cuts off mid-sentence. Emotional beat: the past becoming audible.

chapters.title: Aldous Smiles
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The vice principal, charming and cornered, notices Jonah's snooping and offers him a college recommendation and a spot on the tech crew for the audition night—generosity with hooks in it. Jonah accepts, hating himself. Emotional beat: corruption as kindness.

chapters.title: Third Note: The Lake House
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ghost's note gives an address. Jonah and Dev, who has now been sworn in, find the boarded-up lake house where, per a hidden scrapbook, Marisol drowned at a board-member's party while adults delayed calling for help to protect their careers. Emotional beat: grief without a body to mourn at.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Stalls
chapters.summary: Rosa Vega's POV, revealed to readers but not Jonah. Rosa, the school's night custodian, has been leaving the notes using a chemistry trick she and Marisol invented—she is the ghost. Watching Jonah from the wings, she wonders if he has the nerve she needs, or if he'll fold like everyone else. Emotional beat: a vigilante's loneliness.

chapters.title: Loyalty Test
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ostrander summons Jonah, reveals he knows about @hallwayghost, and offers a deal: delete the account and a full ride appears; keep posting and Jonah's own buried secrets—hacked grade changes he made sophomore year—go to the district. Emotional beat: power showing its true face.

chapters.title: What the Account Knows
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev discovers Jonah is @hallwayghost and feels betrayed by every anonymous post that used his private confessions as content. Their friendship cracks in the AV closet where it was built. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that wounds the wielder.

chapters.title: Priya Runs the Story
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya publishes the Vega name in the school paper; the issue is confiscated within an hour by order of the board, and her press credentials are suspended. She realizes the confiscation order is signed by Aldous—her own mentor. Emotional beat: disillusionment sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Fourth Note: A Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ghost's note names the surviving witness to the lake house cover-up: Aldous, who was then a young chaperone who drove Marisol home that night and stayed silent. The note's ink, for the first time, looks faded—human. Emotional beat: the ghost becoming a person.

chapters.title: Aldous Breaks
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Cornered by Jonah with the tape and the note, Aldous confesses: he was ordered to stay quiet, was promoted for it, and has hated himself for fifteen years. He gives Jonah the original incident report he kept as insurance. Emotional beat: complicity and its slow poison.

chapters.title: Deleted
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ostrander makes good on his threat: the district announces an investigation into 'grade irregularities' targeting Jonah, and his college acceptance is provisionally revoked. Dev and Priya, despite everything, show up at his door with the confiscated newspapers. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing itself.

chapters.title: The Plan in the AV Closet
chapters.summary: Jonah, Dev, and Priya's interleaved POVs. They plan to hijack the audition night's livestream—the tech crew is Jonah's—to broadcast the incident report, the tape, and the scrubbed archives between acts. Rosa leaves them a final note: 'She wanted to be heard. Make it loud.' Emotional beat: fear becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Audition night, the auditorium packed, the board in the front row. As Ostrander takes the stage to dedicate the arts wing, Jonah cuts the feed to the incident report. The room erupts; Aldous, on stage, confirms it aloud. Emotional beat: the silence breaking.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wanted
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. In the chaos, Rosa takes the stage and tells the audience who she is and who her sister was. Ostrander resigns that night; the investigation into the cover-up begins. She finds Jonah backstage and, for the first time, they speak as allies instead of notes. Emotional beat: mourning finally allowed.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah faces his own reckoning—suspension for the grade changes, the revoked acceptance, a district hearing—but Priya's published investigation reframes him as a whistleblower, and a state university offers him a place. He deletes @hallwayghost voluntarily. Emotional beat: accountability without shame.

chapters.title: Ordinary Ink
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. Months later, at the renamed Marisol Vega Black Box Theater's opening, Jonah finds a last note in his locker—his own name, in plain ballpoint: 'Thanks for listening. — R.' Dev drags him onstage for the curtain call, and this time he doesn't hide. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and accepted.
